Professor's note, second-year engineering, Mechanics, November.
Varun came to my office nine days before the end-semester exam. He told me he had not understood anything since the chapter on rotational motion in August, almost three months ago. He had stopped attending tutorials in September because, in his words, "everyone would see I was lost". His classmate Avni had noticed and urged him to come earlier; he kept saying next week. He was ashamed, and it showed: he could barely look up. Nine days is not enough to rebuild three months. I have given him two extra sessions and a list of priority topics, and told him plainly that coming in August would have made this far easier.

passage:
Dear Diary, 2 December.
Exam in six days. Today I finally told Madhuri I haven't understood organic chemistry since the first unit. She stared at me. "Since July? Pooja, why didn't you say?" Because she's the smart one, and I didn't want her to know. Because every week I thought I'd catch up alone. Because it was embarrassing.
She sat with me for two hours. We did one chapter. There are seven. She was kind, but I could see her calculating how impossible it is. I felt so ashamed I wanted to disappear.
If I'd said something in July, it would have been one chapter at a time.
Pooja

qa.a: Madhuri is shocked and kind, but also worried, knowing how little time is left to help.

passage: The photocopy shop near the bus stand in Malerkotla was where the college seniors sat in the evenings. Three days before the cost accounting exam, Hafsa finally went there, her file clutched to her chest. She had missed most of October helping in her family's bangle shop during the wedding rush, and every week since, she had meant to catch up. Every week the pile looked more embarrassing. When classmates asked, she said, "Almost done revising." Nilesh, the senior who tutored, flipped through her half-empty notebook. "Hafsa, six chapters? In three days?" She stared at the floor. "I know." He was kind about it, but honest. "I can take you through two properly. Marginal costing and budgets carry the most marks. The rest you'll have to skim." Walking home past the closed shutters, she worked it out herself: back in early November, one hour a week would have been enough.

qa.a: She could have told Nilesh or a teacher right after the wedding rush that she had missed October, when an hour a week would have been enough.
